Before deciding that two pictures are equivalent, the reader has to know what is permitted: stretching, sliding, bending, dividing a surface, attaching a piece, crossing through, moving endpoints, or preserving boundaries. The reader also has to know what is not permitted. Endpoints may have to stay on named boundary points. A gluing rule may have to stay attached. Two paths may be forbidden to cross. A collision state may have been removed from the model. Changing any one of those rules changes the problem. A knot is only knotted because passing through itself is forbidden; a disk path puzzle is only obstructed because paths may not cross.

They are the same under a stated kind of motion. A loop may be the same after bending but not after breaking. A surface may be the same after stretching but not after changing an edge identification.
